Class LastAdminGuard

java.lang.Object
org.jwcarman.who.admin.LastAdminGuard
public final class LastAdminGuard extends Object
Keeps who's admin endpoints from leaving no active identity that holds WhoAdminPermissions.IDENTITIES_MANAGE. Deactivating an identity and removing one of its roles run through it; a change that would take the holders from one or more to none is refused with LastAdminException. When no one holds the permission, nothing is refused.

Holders are counted from who-rbac's tables: the ACTIVE identities assigned a role that carries the permission. Only who-rbac's resolver makes those the holders, so the guard is enforcing only when the application's permissions come from who-rbac. With a resolver of the application's own, who cannot tell who holds the permission, so the guard refuses nothing rather than refuse on a count it cannot trust; who's autoconfiguration logs a warning at startup when that is so.

The lock. The count and the change run in one transaction that first locks, with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, every who_role row whose role carries the permission, in id order. Every guarded change takes those same locks, so two of them cannot both count before either changes: two admins demoting each other, or one deactivating the other while being demoted, are serialized, and the second counts what the first committed. The role rows are the narrowest thing every such change has in common: an identity's own row would not serialize changes to two different identities, and a table lock would also stop unrelated writes. A concurrent assignment of one of those roles waits for the lock briefly, which only adds a holder. The transaction is READ COMMITTED whatever the database's default, so the second change counts what the first committed once it has the locks; under REPEATABLE READ it would count its own older snapshot. Called inside a transaction of the caller's, the guard joins it at that transaction's isolation, and the guarantee then needs that transaction to be READ COMMITTED; the admin endpoints call it outside any transaction. Changes made outside the admin endpoints, such as RbacService or WhoService.deactivate called by the application, are not guarded.

      public LastAdminGuard(org.springframework.jdbc.core.simple.JdbcClient jdbcClient, org.springframework.transaction.PlatformTransactionManager transactionManager, boolean enforcing)
      Creates the guard.
      Parameters:
      jdbcClient - reads who-rbac's tables and takes the locks; its data source must be the one transactionManager manages, or the locks are taken outside the transaction
      transactionManager - runs the count and the change in one READ COMMITTED transaction
      enforcing - whether the permission's holders are who-rbac's to count; when false the guard refuses nothing
